key_insight: Unit shows that a small dependent-type checker with uniform definition handling can support substantial formal mathematics without tactics, unification, or instance search.
engineering_relevance: Its explicit checking process offers a simpler architecture for proof-checking tools whose behavior can be inspected alongside informal proofs.
method: Use dependent type theory with an Automath-style module system.
Compare definitions by name and arguments before unfolding; otherwise unfold the most recently declared definition.
Avoid unification, instance search, tactics, and unfolding heuristics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports checked developments covering a model of univalent type theory, synthetic algebraic geometry through Châtelet’s theorem, and synthetic Stone duality with its cohomology, but gives no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The lack of proof automation may increase manual proof-authoring effort; the abstract does not quantify this trade-off.
paper_title: Unit: a type checker for dependent type theory
